7ffce60d59361fc2: LONDON: Mauricio Pochettino starts his Manchester United career with a baptism of fire at the home of bitter rivals Liverpool this weekend, tasked with lifting a dysfunctional side out of the Premier League relegation zone.
The Red Devils could be rock bottom of the table by the time they kick off, depending on results elsewhere, and the Anfield crowd will relish their predicament.
Elsewhere, second-placed Brighton are seeking a seventh win in eight league games as they try to stay in touch with leaders Arsenal, while Manchester City are desperate to end their slump.
AFP Sport looks at three talking points ahead of the action:
Pochettino magic?
Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of his new club at Anfield just days after wrapping up his reign as US coach.
In some ways the immediate pressure is off the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss – a win at Liverpool would be considered a huge bonus.
But victory would give him instant momentum as he fights to lift the club up the table.
Results so far this season under the now-departed Michael Carrick have been historically bad.
United's tally of eight points after 10 games is their lowest at this stage of a league season for 40 years.
Fixtures after their Anfield trip – against Brentford, Newcastle, Coventry and Crystal Palace – look easier on paper but United have a solitary win in their first 10 league games.
Pochettino says he needs time to turn the club's fortunes around but he will be aware of the need to show progress quickly.
Man City slump
Manchester City have lost their past three Premier League matches after racing out of the blocks with seven straight wins.
The early pacesetters are already six points behind leaders and defending champions Arsenal.
But Enzo Maresca's men are in the curious psychological position of knowing even if they close the gap, it might ultimately all be in vain.

The 10-time English champions are still waiting to discover their fate after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules – with a huge points deduction one potential punishment.
If they could choose an opponent to help end their slump, it would probably be Fulham.
Incredibly, City have won their past 20 matches against the London team in all competitions.
And their 17-game winning streak against the London side in the league is the longest in the history of the English top flight.
Brighton charge
Brighton midfielder Pascal Gross was reluctant to entertain talk of a title challenge after their 2-0 victory against Brentford before the international break.
"No, we are not in a title race," the 35-year-old told Sky Sports. "But we have started the season really well. It's the beginning of the season.
"You see the Premier League, the margins and you look at the results – we are not getting carried away yet."
But the south-coast side are now second favourites with British bookmakers to be crowned champions for the first time in their history.

Seven of Brighton's opening 10 games have come against teams who finished in the top 10 last season, including fixtures against the top two, Arsenal and Man City. Brighton won both of those without conceding a goal.
The Seagulls are the league's top scorers with 26 goals, 11 more than Arsenal, and have the second-tightest defence, with just seven goals conceded.
They will fancy their chances on Saturday against Hull, who have not won a Premier League match since August.
Brighton's highest-ever finish in the Premier League was sixth in the 2022/23 season but Fabian Hurzeler's men are well on track to break new ground. - AFP

98e8bc799787697f: PETALING JAYA: Former MP Charles Santiago has urged Putrajaya to clarify its position on reintegrating junta-led Myanmar into Asean following yesterday’s ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) that the country committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ found that Myanmar’s military killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, committed widespread sexual violence, subjected children to extreme violence, attacked people fleeing their homes and destroyed villages.
The court also found that these acts were committed with the specific intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population.

Santiago, co-chairman of the Asean Parliamentarians for Human Rights, said Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s decision to welcome junta leader Min Aung Hlaing to Malaysia on Oct 8 had become harder to defend following the ruling.
He also said Anwar’s assurance to Min Aung Hlaing that Malaysia would explore ways to facilitate Myanmar’s return to Asean was deeply troubling in light of the court’s findings.
"What exactly is Malaysia seeking to rehabilitate: a military regime whose conduct has now been recognised as genocide by an international court?" he said in a statement.

"The ICJ has spoken. Now the world must act. And Malaysia, having chosen to extend a state welcome to Min Aung Hlaing and promised to help bring his regime back into Asean, must decide which side of history it intends to stand on."
ICJ judges, led by court president Yuji Iwasawa, ordered Myanmar to "allow and facilitate the safe, voluntary and dignified return" of Rohingya who had fled the violence to their homes.
The judges also ordered Myanmar to investigate and punish those suspected of committing genocide, with compensation to be determined at a later date.

Santiago said Myanmar’s reintegration into the regional bloc must be conditional on concrete political and institutional reforms, an end to violence, meaningful engagement with all stakeholders and compliance with international obligations.
"Offering legitimacy before accountability is not diplomacy but appeasement. For Asean, the ICJ judgment must be a turning point," he said.
"The organisation cannot issue statements welcoming the decision and then carry on with business as usual.
"It must use its collective diplomatic and political influence to compel Myanmar to comply with the court’s orders."

1d104f18c38c8638: SHENZEN: Reporters traveling with US President Donald Trump were asked to surrender cell phones they had used in China in a rare security precaution as Air Force One prepared to leave Shenzhen on Thursday.

"A staffer collected a number of cellphones from poolers when we got on the plane and placed them in a Faraday bag, designed to block signal," a White House pool reporter said in a note upon returning to the US.
"This was explained to us as being a necessary cybersecurity precaution against potential spying attempts," the report added.
According to the separate video pool report, a presidential aide collected temporary "burner" phones used by White House staff during the China visit for disposal or data wiping.
Journalists were asked to place devices they had used in the country into signal-blocking bags until the aircraft landed in the US.
The so-called Faraday bags are designed to shield electronic devices from wireless communications, reducing the risk of surveillance or data collection.
Burner phones are temporary devices used in place of regular cell phones to protect them from potential security threats.
The video pool report said many reporters and photographers had left their regular work and personal phones, laptops and smart watches inside the protective bags before landing in China on Wednesday.
Those devices were not collected and could be used on the return flight, while journalists who had relied on their regular cell phones during the visit were left without them.
The phones were returned to the pool reporters upon Air Force One landing stateside.
The unusual precautions followed Trump's meetings with world leaders in Shenzhen, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
b4520b3782caf93b: PARIS: Ireland host South Africa in their Nations Championship Test on Saturday and risk getting a "full blast" from a Springbok side bruised by defeat by France and furious at their coach Rassie Erasmus being banned, Irish rugby great Hugo MacNeill told AFP.

The world champions will travel one person light to Lansdowne Road, with Erasmus banned for six matches following incendiary remarks about the match officials in last Saturday's pulsating 21-19 loss to the French.
Erasmus said the officials' decisions amounted to "match-fixing."
"That was really bad, really poor," MacNeill told AFP by phone, referring to Erasmus's outburst.
"It's a bad thing for the game, being so critical. The Springboks, though, might use that as a bit of motivation themselves, that they have been treated unfairly.
"Ironically, him not being there may have a bigger impact, but in terms of firing them up."

There is more at stake in this November's meeting between the two sides than last year's chaotic Test. The Irish were down to 12 men at one stage and the Springboks won 24-13 for their first win in Dublin since 2012.
Both countries are still in the running to top their respective pools and play in the final on Finals weekend, which begins on Friday week, at Twickenham.
MacNeill, a dashing fullback and key member of two Triple Crown-winning sides in 1982 and 1985, believes a bruised Springboks side is a fearsome prospect.
However, the Irish come into the game boosted by two victories by large margins, beating Argentina 42-12 and Fiji 43-15.
"Being realistic, going up against the world champions who have just been beaten and are furious with the referees, Ireland risk receiving a full blast from the 'Boks," said MacNeill.
"The question is can they match that and stand up to it.
"We won't outmuscle them so will our back line be coherent like the French were? For me, we don't have that."

MacNeill, who put his own Test career on the line when in 1981 he refused to tour South Africa because of the apartheid regime, said Ireland's lack of a world class fly-half since iconic playmaker Johnny Sexton retired following the 2023 World Cup was preventing them from being considered contenders to win next year's Rugby World Cup.
- 'Coherent backplay' -

Ireland coach Andy Farrell, who has admitted his side are not as strong as they were a year out from the 2023 World Cup, looked to have resolved the issue when Jack Crowley produced some impressive performances in steering the Irish to the Six Nations Triple Crown last season.
However, he has been laid low since April with a rare vascular lower limb injury, which MacNeill concedes is a "blow", so Sam Prendergast has stepped in.
"It is fair to say we are yet to unearth somebody who can do what he (Sexton) did," said MacNeill.
"We have been trying different people but they have not been convincing and primarily lack the consistency of Sexton.
"If you don't have that key player it curtails what you can do and achieve," added the 68-year-old.
MacNeill, who also won three British and Irish Lions caps, said Ireland had been spoilt in having Sexton, who followed another world-class fly-half in Ronan O'Gara.
"When O'Gara went you had Sexton snapping at his heels," said MacNeill.
"When he went we didn't have that. When Ireland have won things we had a coherent backplay thanks to top class fly-halves like Ollie Campbell and Tony Ward.
"We just don't have that for the moment, those players are not around."
MacNeill says Ireland are a decent side and Prendergast is a good player but he has yet to put together an impressive all-round performance.
"He is very slight and as a result his defence is a worry," said MacNeill.
"Clearly the Springboks bring immense physicality right through the side which is hard to match.
"Ireland have to step up or it will be a very tough day." - AFP

2a318e075b33693a: HONG KONG: Tech firms led losses across Asia once again Friday as Anthropic's sparkling debut failed to muster a recovery in sentiment towards the artificial intelligence (AI) trade, with nerves frayed by worries over crisis-hit Nvidia, profitability and regulation.
After its record-breaking initial public offering, Claude-creator Anthropic soared 17 per cent on its first day as ordinary investors sought to grab a piece of the new kid on the block.
But the rally did nothing to drag other, more established firms higher as the uncertainty that has hung over the tech sector in recent months sapped confidence, sending Wall Street deep into the red.

Magnificent Seven members who led a scorching surge over the past two years continued a retreat that has characterised trade since the summer, as investors fret over AI profitability, eye-watering spending, rising borrowing costs and geopolitics.

Microsoft, Apple, Amazon and Tesla were all well down, along with Nvidia -- which is battling to deal with the fallout from a spy scandal that has led to the resignation of pivotal leader Jensen Huang.
The losses continued on US futures markets, with Anthropic dropping more than four per cent.

Traders have also been spooked by the US Commerce Department's move to close a loophole allowing Chinese companies to access Nvidia's powerful AI chips remotely, adding to worries that a new Democratic-led Congress will impose further regulations.
The selling followed through to Asia, where Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei -- home to the region's leading AI-linked firms -- tumbled between four and six per cent.

Japan's Nikkei 225 was dragged by losses of more than 10 per cent in Kioxia, Advantest and tech investor SoftBank, TSMC shed 4.5 per cent and MediaTek tanked 9.4 per cent as Taiwan's main stock market was dragged five per cent lower.
SK hynix and Samsung were around six per cent down as South Korea's Kospi dived more than four per cent.
Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore and Manila also took a pummelling.

"With volatility elevated, equity futures breaking support and high-beta assets under pressure, traders will increasingly look for signs of capitulation, stabilisation or a catalyst capable of reversing sentiment," said Chris Weston at Pepperstone.
"The risk is that selling becomes self-reinforcing. As volatility rises, risk limits tighten, leveraged positions are reduced and systematic strategies can add to the pressure.

"Whether Anthropic's IPO proves to be a defining moment for the AI trade remains to be seen. For now, the immediate priority is watching how markets settle into the weekend and whether buyers can regain control next week."

Investors are keeping tabs on developments in the Nvidia case as California announced it was investigating whether the firm misled the public and investors about its chips ending up in China, despite federal export controls.
Huang resigned last week after reports alleged he had multiple extramarital affairs, including with a woman named Alice Huang who is a suspected Chinese spy.

Alice Huang, who is no relation, is the former director of Megaspeed, a cloud computing company based in Singapore that was investigated by local officials in 2025 over potential export control violations.
Jensen Huang has agreed to attend a closed-door questioning session about national security issues with Congressional officials on Dec 1.
Oil prices edged up after the International Energy Agency (IEA) said the crisis in the Middle East had created the "largest threat" to energy security in history.
The IEA said in its annual World Energy Outlook that consumers were increasingly footing the bill as the world runs out of ways to absorb the impact of the conflict on energy supplies.

44537854150e2437: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will end visa-free entry for Indian citizens on Dec 31.
In a written parliamentary reply to Datuk Seri Dr Ismail Abd Muttalib (Maran), the Home Ministry said the move was intended to strengthen pre-arrival screening and improve entry controls.
The visa exemption was initially introduced for one year, until Dec 31, 2024, before being extended for another two years to cover Indian and Chinese citizens.

It allowed eligible Indian visitors to enter Malaysia without a visa for stays of up to 30 days for tourism, business and social visits, subject to immigration requirements. Employment and study were not permitted.
The Immigration Department recorded 916,821 Indian visitors in the first year of the exemption, a 223 per cent increase from 2023.
The ministry said the government had adopted a three-pronged approach covering pre-arrival screening, checks upon arrival and enforcement against foreigners already in the country.
Other measures included ending the Multiple Entry Visa facility for short-term social visits by citizens of visa-exempt countries, including China, from Sept 1.
The restriction was intended to prevent repeated visits from being used for illegal employment or business activities.

e1cff447002ca61c: SYDNEY: Pat Cummins is widely regarded as an all-round nice guy with an excellent cricketing brain, but the Australian Test captain's reputation has taken a huge hit over the past week and he risks becoming the next victim of "Sandpapergate."
Cummins is enmeshed in fresh allegations around the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, with claims that he and other team members lied about what they knew.
It blew up anew on November 7 when retired opener Usman Khawaja, ahead of the release of his autobiography, said the "whole team" were aware of the plot to alter the ball in a Test at Cape Town.
Only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were deemed responsible by a Cricket Australia probe.

During a lengthy press conference a week ago Cummins vehemently denied he knew anything, only for Bancroft – the player tasked with using sandpaper – to relight the fuse by backing Khawaja's version of events.
It has left Australia's top-earning cricketer under siege, with calls for him to step down.
Cummins has been central to changing the Australian team's culture and standing since being appointed skipper in 2021.
"I just can't see how his captaincy and personal brand survives this," former Australia quick Mitchell Johnson wrote in a column for The West Australian newspaper.
Another ex-Australian fast bowler, Jason Gillespie, told broadcaster ABC: "It's a very awkward situation for Pat Cummins."
Cummins and the bowling group of Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon have maintained all along that they only learned of the use of sandpaper when Bancroft was caught.
Cricket Australia has so far stood behind the 33-year-old Cummins.
But a poll by The Australian newspaper this week of 13,000 voters showed 82 percent believed Bancroft and Khawaja.
If Cummins were to step aside as captain, there is no clear-cut replacement.
Smith has routinely filled the role when Cummins was absent, but he too is intricately entwined in "Sandpapergate."
Travis Head is the other deputy, while Alex Carey is considered a calm and measured voice.
- Fiery welcome -
It is a major headache for Australian cricket ahead of a home four-Test series against New Zealand in December-January, followed by two massive tours of India and old enemy England.
The New Zealand series opens in Perth, home to Bancroft, where the reaction of the crowd could be telling.
Cummins and the Australia team can expect a fiery welcome by England fans when they contest the Ashes.
Test great Ian Healy implored Cummins to speak again to shore up his leadership.
"If Pat doesn't address it I think I would struggle to have him in front of a team meeting at the start of a Test and running the show," he told reporters, referring to Bancroft's claims.

Earmarked as a potential star from a young age, Cummins burst on the scene aged 18, taking seven wickets to set up a two-wicket win and earn man-of-the match in a Test against South Africa in Johannesburg in 2011.
He also made waves for New South Wales and in the Twenty20 Big Bash League, but then came the injuries that prevented him from playing another Test for six long years.
A series of stress fractures in his lower back derailed his career and plagued him with doubts.
He emerged from those dark times – and the pain and rehab that went with it – a stronger person and cricketer and his persistence saw him selected again for Australia's tour of India in 2017.

Cummins came through that sub-continental test unscathed and quickly became a mainstay in all three formats alongside Hazlewood and Starc – not only a consistent and reliable paceman but a devastating one.
He was elevated to vice-skipper in 2019 and the captaincy in 2021 when Tim Paine was forced out over a sexting scandal.
Since then he has been widely praised for his captaincy abilities, redefining the Australian team culture while maintaining a winning mentality.
All that hard work, and his legacy, are now under threat. - AFP

83b22ecd44577ce0: NEW YORK/LONDON: Citigroup underestimated its risk-weighted assets (RWA) after an error in recording some trades, according to people familiar with the matter, forcing the US lender to inject capital into a subsidiary.

It is a setback for the US lender that is seeking to rapidly address years-long regulatory demands and represents another challenge for Citi chief executive officer Jane Fraser, who has been trying to fix various problems at the bank for years.

Citi has operated under tight supervisory scrutiny in the US, and as recently as the summer was targeting submitting paperwork to regulators this year to get the restrictions lifted, Reuters has reported.
The bank underestimated the risk-weighted assets by about US$35 billion at a trading unit in Europe, one person familiar with the matter said.

The bank recorded some trades incorrectly, which meant it underestimated its risk-weighted assets, two people said. The size of RWA is a key measure used by regulators to determine how much capital banks need to hold as a buffer for potential losses.

In a statement to Reuters, Citigroup said the bank had identified and resolved an internal capital modeling issue at a European trading subsidiary this summer. "The subsidiary remained fully compliant with regulatory minimums throughout, with no impact on the holding company or main operating bank," the bank said.
"Citi completed remedial actions and injected capital to immediately restore the subsidiary's buffers."

The Wall Street firm incorrectly recorded trades at its UK securities unit using an internal model based on its own statistical assumptions, the people said. Regulators had not approved the model for those types of transactions, they added. Once the trades were recorded using a standard risk model, the value of RWAs shot up significantly, the people said.

The third-largest US bank reported about US$1.2 trillion of total RWA in June and September, filings show, indicating the error represented about 2.7 per cent of the total. Reuters could not establish if the bank has already reflected the adjustment to RWA in the reported figures.

Citi's problems stretch back to 2020, when it was told to remediate longstanding risk management and data governance problems identified by the US Federal Reserve and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

The bank was fined US$400 million and agreed to a long list of longstanding issues it needed to fix, but was then fined another US$136 million in 2024 for the delay in fixing its data management problems.
The Federal Reserve had no comment on the underestimation of RWA when contacted by Reuters. The comptroller could not be immediately reached outside regular business hours.
Shaking off the regulatory shackles would free up resources, become a key achievement for Fraser and bolster Citigroup shares, according to analysts.

The bank has also been reprimanded for breaches in Europe. In 2024, UK regulators fined Citigroup the equivalent of US$78.5 million for controls failings in its trading operations, one of the biggest sanctions for systems breaches. In one of the blunders, Citi had caused a sudden fall in European stocks in May 2022.
Separately, Britain's Prudential Regulation Authority had fined the bank US$56.3 million in 2019 for providing inaccurate financial statements.

c9b6d49e6d93cc28: LAS VEGAS: Heavy rain, standing water and frigid temperatures left Formula One teams with little reason to take risks in Thursday's opening practice for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with no driver setting a timed lap.

2ff05476ef968c61: SYDNEY: A data centre planned in regional Australia with Anthropic as its anchor tenant is overwhelmingly opposed by residents, a filing for the project showed, setting the scene for a showdown between the AI company and the community hosting its first Australian facility.

Of nearly 600 public submissions on the proposed Western Downs Digital Park, about 250 km (155 miles) west of Brisbane, two expressed support for the project and one was neutral, according to the filing. The remaining 595 opposed it or asked for a delay until developers cleared certain environmental hurdles, the filing said.
"A significant number of submissions raise reasonable matters regarding water, power, noise, roads, housing and the scale of the project," the filing, lodged on behalf of developer Zerra DC, said.
Representatives of Zerra and Anthropic were not immediately available for comment.

The initial response, though far from binding, gives a sense of the souring relationship between communities and the so-called AI factories being built at pace around the world in a boom McKinsey has valued at US$7 trillion by 2030.

Already in Australia, Goodman Group scrapped a roughly A$1.2 billion data centre planned for Sydney in September after a public backlash, while NextDC delayed a project in Melbourne amid resident concerns about energy use, triggering a shares selldown.

The Anthropic project is on farmland and further from the suburbs, but with a planned computing load of 1.44 gigawatts would be one of the country's biggest. About one-third of the submissions were from people who lived within 200 km of the site, the filing said.
Objectors mostly cited concerns about water use, electricity demand and prices, noise, road damage from construction traffic and pressure on housing.

Before the data centre project named Anthropic as its tenant on Sept 15, it had received five objections in a month, a log of public comments showed, with the rest arriving between then and Nov 11, when the local government stopped accepting submissions.

The filing about Australian data centre submissions was published the same week Anthropic made its stock market debut on Wall St, pricing its initial public offering on Nov 18 in a deal that valued the company at around US$1.5 trillion.

dd6f750cca9d43d3: TOKYO: Inflation in Japan picked up again in October due to rising food prices and energy costs, official data showed Friday, boosting the likelihood of an interest rate hike.
Excluding volatile fresh produce, inflation was 2.2%, up from 2.1% in September, according to the internal affairs ministry reading.
The latest figure is slightly below the 2.3% expected by experts surveyed by Bloomberg.
Soaring energy costs due to the Middle East conflict as well as a weak yen are pushing up prices of imported products, including food.
Energy prices also rose sharply as the government scaled back subsidies for gasoline and electricity that had helped mitigate the impact of the war.
The cost of electricity rose 1.6% in October from a year ago, compared to a drop of 2.4% in September, while the price of gas jumped 5.3% compared with a 0.2% rise.
Marcel Thieliant of Capital Economics said the subsidy scale back had played a role as "electricity inflation turned positive for the first time in a year".
"While the government will reinstate subsidies over the winter, those subsidies aren't any more generous than usual," he said.
"With unsubsidised tariffs reaching a record high, utilities prices will soon rise at a double-digit pace".
Prime minister Sanae Takaichi has pledged another round of subsidies to meet rising energy demand in winter, while also pushing a two-year consumption tax cut scheme for food from next year.
Still, analysts have noted the persistent weakness of the yen as a key factor boosting consumer prices.

The Bank of Japan declared last month that inflation had hit its two percent target, and is expected to trend "clearly above 2 percent" in months to come, driven by rising prices of a wide range of products and services, including those related to artificial intelligence demand, such as semiconductors.
The inflation figure Friday is likely to strengthen the central bank's case for further tightening of monetary policy.
Japanese officials are expected to hike interest rates in December as inflationary pressure builds.

5bfa495a8a36b508: MADRID: Real Madrid have cut the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona down to three points, without the help of Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior, who faces a fight to reclaim his place in the team.

Los Blancos have the chance to pull provisionally level with the Catalan giants on Saturday when they host Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu, with Vinicius in contention to play after serving a four-match domestic ban for hair-pulling.
In Vinicius's absence Jose Mourinho's side beat champions Barca in the Clasico at Camp Nou, as well as scoring wins over Sevilla, Racing Santander and Valencia.

The forward started in Madrid's Champions League victories over AEK Athens and RB Leipzig in that period but without finding the form which made him a vital player for Los Blancos over the past few years.
Vinicius, who joined Real Madrid from Flamengo in 2018, carved out a reputation as one of the most dangerous attackers in world football, helping his side win the Champions League in 2022 and 2024.
However, this season he has struggled badly for form, with his only Madrid goal coming in August against Real Sociedad.
In the interim period Madrid's record signing Yan Diomande has adapted well to his new club and has four goals in his last eight appearances, staking his claim for the left wing spot.
During the international break Vinicius found some relief with Brazil, led by former Madrid coach Carlo Ancelotti.
The forward seemed unlocked, scoring five times in two friendlies against Japan and Singapore, which he hopes can be a platform to turn his domestic form around.
Vinicius admitted this summer, during which he was heavily linked with a departure from Madrid before ultimately penning a new deal until 2032, he let his standards slip.
Brazil suffered a surprise round-of-16 elimination at the World Cup by Erling Haaland's Norway, which took a toll.

"I don't think I prepared myself as well as I could have after the World Cup because the impact of that tournament is very significant for all Brazilians... being knocked out so early was something we didn't expect," he told reporters this week.
"I used the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years."
Vinicius said speculation on his future led to him feeling "overwhelmed" and he also highlighted the difficulty of staying at the peak of the game.
"I think only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to do it for so many years, reaching the same numbers," he added.
"I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve."
- Change of scene -
Vinicius's only other goal this season came in the previous international break, for Brazil against Australia in a friendly.
Former Real Madrid player Predrag Mijatovic told Spanish radio station Cadena Ser that Vinicius seems happier playing for Brazil than his club side.

"I think last summer hurt Vinicius quite a bit because he had that doubt about whether to stay or not, whether to renew his contract or not, and he has more competition this year, right?" said Mijatovic.
"Diomande is performing well in this position, and now Mourinho is the one who has to make his own decisions.
"What's clear is that Vini performs well when he's happy, and I see him much happier playing with his national team than playing here."
In previous campaigns the Brazilian has saved his best form for the second half of the season.
"Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals," said Vinicius.
In each of the past five seasons he has netted at least 22 times for Madrid.
On occasion Vinicius has faced criticism and whistles from the team's own fans, but Mourinho has shown patience, while urging the most lethal version of the forward to return.
"The Vini who is at his best kills games – like he killed me in the past when I was with Benfica," said the veteran Portuguese coach in September.
Mourinho will hope that Vinicius's joy with Brazil can reignite his club form and bring back that killer instinct. - AFP

0bf3ef87a85b0370: KUALA LUMPUR: Emirates has carried nearly 12 million passengers to and from Malaysia over the past three decades as the Dubai-based airline prepares to increase seat capacity on its Kuala Lumpur route with a second daily Airbus A380 from Dec 1.

Emirates country manager in Malaysia Saeed Mubarak said the airline had expanded from three weekly flights when it entered the Malaysian market in October 1996 to 21 weekly services today, while increasing its cargo capacity and introducing newer aircraft and cabin products.

"Our growth in Malaysia over the past three decades is reflected in the expansion of our flight frequency, aircraft deployment and cargo capacity, alongside our continued investment in connectivity and the customer experience," he told Business Times in an interview recently.
Emirates' cumulative figures showed that the airline had operated 44,312 flights and transported some 335 million kilogrammes of cargo to and from Malaysia between Oct 1996 and Oct 2026.
The airline began operations in Malaysia on Oct 27, 1996, with three weekly flights from Dubai to Kuala Lumpur via Dhaka, using a Boeing 777-200.
It currently operates three daily nonstop flights between Kuala Lumpur and Dubai using an A380, an A350 and a retrofitted B777-300ER.
Saeed said the airline will replace its daily B777-300ER service with a second A380 from Dec 1 to accommodate passenger demand during the winter travel season.
The additional A380 will feature First Class, Business Class and Economy Class cabins, while the A350 will continue operating on the route.
The change will increase seat capacity without adding to Emirates' existing three daily frequencies.

Saeed said passenger demand between Malaysia and Dubai is supported by Malaysian outbound travellers, international visitors travelling to Malaysia and passengers connecting through Dubai to destinations across Emirates' global network.

Dubai remained a destination for Malaysian travellers visiting for leisure, shopping and business, while also providing connections to over 130 destinations worldwide, including cities in Europe, the Americas, Africa and the Middle East.
He said inbound tourism is another important market segment, with Emirates working with Tourism Malaysia to promote the country's attractions among travellers across its network.
On the airline's forward bookings, Saeed said Emirates has reported positive trends for the winter travel season across its global network with several markets tracking ahead of the previous year.
Between July and August 2026, Emirates carried more than 8.6 million passengers globally while maintaining healthy seat load factors.
Saeed said the airline continues to operate its three daily Kuala Lumpur-Dubai flights despite geopolitical tensions and airspace restrictions affecting aviation operations in the Middle East.

"While geopolitical tensions and airspace restrictions have created challenges for the aviation industry, Emirates has progressively restored its operations and is now operating at around 91–93 per cent of its pre-disruption capacity," he said.
He said passenger safety remained the airline's priority with operations adjusted when necessary according to developments in the region.
Emirates has also introduced more flexible booking arrangements for affected passengers, including date changes without change fees on eligible tickets and reduced refund fees on selected fares.
Passengers whose journeys were disrupted could also receive accommodation assistance and be rebooked to their final destinations, where applicable.
Saeed said competition among international airlines serving the Malaysian market had increased over the years, providing passengers with more choices of airlines, aircraft and connecting hubs.
He said Emirates continues to invest in its aircraft and onboard services to maintain its position in the market, including the introduction of its A350 and retrofitted B777 aircraft.

The airline introduced Premium Economy on its Kuala Lumpur services last year and has received a positive response from Malaysian passengers, particularly those travelling on longer journeys through Dubai to Europe and the Americas.
"Malaysian travellers are particularly value-conscious and consistently seek products and services that offer good value for money," Saeed said.
As of September 2026, Emirates has completed its retrofit programme on 107 aircraft globally, bringing its latest cabin products, including Premium Economy, to 143 aircraft.
The airline is also introducing further onboard improvements, including high-speed Starlink inflight connectivity and upgraded cabin features.
On airfares, Saeed said several factors influenced ticket prices, including jet fuel costs, seasonality and market conditions.

On the possibility of expanding Emirates' operations to other Malaysian cities, Saeed said the airline continues to evaluate network opportunities based on passenger demand, market potential and operational requirements.

"As with all our network decisions, any additional frequencies or new destinations are carefully evaluated before being introduced. We consider several factors with consumer demand and market potential being key considerations," he said.
Emirates currently extends its connectivity beyond Kuala Lumpur through its codeshare partnership with Batik Air Malaysia, which began in October 2023.

The agreement allows Emirates passengers to connect to five domestic destinations, namely Penang, Langkawi, Johor Bahru, Kota Kinabalu and Kuching, as well as three regional destinations — Singapore, Jakarta and Denpasar.
Meanwhile, Saeed said Emirates SkyCargo continues to support Malaysia's international trade through the belly-hold capacity of the airline's three daily widebody passenger flights.
Emirates currently provides close to 700 tonnes of cargo capacity weekly from Malaysia, serving businesses exporting goods to international markets through Dubai.
Malaysia's key outbound commodities include electronics and components, consumer products, aviation and oil and gas spare parts, and renewable energy equipment such as solar panels.

Across East and Southeast Asia, Emirates SkyCargo transported over 439,000 tonnes of cargo from 12 markets in its 2025/2026 financial year, representing about five per cent growth from the previous financial year.
On the possibility of introducing dedicated freighter services to Malaysia, Saeed said any expansion would require an assessment of cargo demand, market conditions and operational requirements.

6aa5797b629559c1: ANTALYA: The UN's COP31 climate talks enter their endgame Friday, with countries sharply divided over a draft deal lacking any mention of planet-heating fossil fuels, threatening to push the negotiations into overtime.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries were scrambling to bridge their differences after two weeks of talks in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya, but the summit appears poised to spill into the weekend.

The talks come with a series of stark reminders of the urgency of climate action, from heatwaves in Europe and devastating floods in Nepal to a record-breaking El Nino wreaking more havoc around the world.
The war in Iran and oil price shock have added another layer of complexity to the talks, sharpening divisions over energy security and the future of fossil fuels.
An initial draft deal earlier this week included calls to accelerate action to phase out fossil fuels.
But a new version released by COP31 co-host Australia on Thursday omitted any mention of oil, gas and coal – the main drivers of climate change.
The absence is a "black mark", French ecological transition minister Monique Barbut said.
"We will be consulting and negotiating until it is very clear to us that we have a consensus," Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who is steering the COP31 negotiations, told reporters.
Electrify the economy

Nations agreed at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels, without setting targets or timelines, and oil-producing countries have fiercely resisted any attempt to bring the issue back to the table.
Last year's summit in Brazil ended without any mention of fossil fuels, prompting countries to pursue their own efforts outside the UN process to exit coal, oil and gas.

"Countries beholden to fossil fuel interests are blocking progress on a fast, fair transition away from fossil fuels," said Rachel Cleetus, climate program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists.
COP31 host Turkey has instead pushed for countries to join a voluntary pledge to increase the global share of final energy demand met by electricity to 35% by 2035.

The draft deal includes a nod to the Turkish initiative, saying that taking steps to electrify the global economy could have "significant benefits" in shoring up energy security and cutting planet-heating greenhouse gas emissions.
Some countries are concerned the text as written does not explicitly require that extra electricity be powered by clean energy and not coal or gas.
"We are going to fight for clean electrification," Barbut said.

Some countries also raised concerns about language welcoming efforts to ramp up carbon capture, utilisation and storage technology, which critics see as an expensive distraction from cutting pollution.
Vanuatu's climate minister Ralph Regenvanu told AFP it "had been singled out for special attention that it doesn't deserve" in the latest text.
Climate science
A fight over climate science has also emerged at COP31.
The timing of the next set of reports by the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has been a source of considerable friction.
The latest text underscores the "importance" of the IPCC.

Dozens of countries want the IPCC's next assessments available before a global review of carbon-cutting efforts in 2028. A smaller number of nations, including Saudi Arabia and India, want them postponed until 2029.
The draft expresses "deep concern" about the imminent breach of the 1.5°C temperature goal set under the 2015 Paris accord.
An age-old fight over money also has yet to be resolved.

Rich nations have resisted calls to increase support for countries struggling to adapt to climate change, citing budget constraints and insisting that big emerging economies such as China also contribute.
The draft proposes further discussions toward "tripling" finance for climate adaptation measures by 2035 but drops a US$120-billion goal being sought by developing nations.
12c39905fb9229cf: KUALA LUMPUR: International fatigue, injuries and boardroom pressure collide as the Super League resumes today after the FIFA break.

While Negri Sembilan and Brunei DPMM enjoyed uninterrupted preparation, Kuching City and Terengganu supplied 14 players for Harimau Malaya's China tour, against China and Yemen, leaving under 72 hours to recover.

Third-placed Kuching City (12 points) visit Paroi for a seventh straight away league match. Despite losing 1-0 to Gangwon in the Asian Champions League Two (ACL 2), they remain buoyed by reaching their maiden FA Cup final at Selangor's expense.

Yet Aidil Sharin Sahak's squad is depleted, with defenders Gabriel Peres (knee) and Jimmy Raymond (broken leg), plus striker Ronald Ngah Wanja (knee), facing lengthy layoffs, while Ajdin Mujagic, Ahmad Israiwah and Joao Pedro are also sidelined.
With six players returning from China and Safawi Rasid leaving camp early for family reasons, Aidil remains defiant.
"We don't complain about the schedule; instead we respect the fixtures set and focus on preparing the team," he said.
Negri (eighth, five points) are fresher, having kept Akhyar Rashid and Luqman Hakim Shamsuddin in camp, and will be looking to build on their earlier league win.
Coach Daniel Gimenez, whose side have failed to beat Kuching in their last six meetings, wants sharper finishing after losing 3–1 to DPMM.
"You can keep the ball and play pretty football, but if you don't score, you lose. That is what is happening to us," he said.
At Gong Badak, Terengganu coach Nafuzi Zain is under siege after five winless league games left the Turtles ninth (five points) and triggered a formal club warning letter on Nov 6.
Suspended strikers Romel Morales and Gervane Kastaneer miss out, while six teammates return from China.
Fourth-placed DPMM (12 points) return rested after 12 days off following their 6–1 FA Cup defeat to Johor Darul Ta'zim, and back to the venue where they stunned Terengganu 3–1 in September.
With newly cleared Malaysian-heritage striker Rodrigo Holgado short of match fitness, Jordan Murray and Dalberto Luan lead the line as coach Jamie McAllister draws on that cup triumph.
"Terengganu have real quality players, but we came with the belief that we could keep going and get through to the next round," he said.
39504033af8a0698: TAMPA: A US judge in Florida on Thursday declared Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Britain's Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Markle, to be mentally competent to answer to a federal court charge accusing him of being a child sexual predator.

Accepting the findings of a court-appointed forensic psychiatrist, US Magistrate Judge Lindsay Griffin ruled the 82-year-old father-in-law of Prince Harry was mentally fit to understand the proceedings against him and to properly assist in his own defense, court records showed.

Neither prosecutors nor the defense disputed the findings of the psychiatrist's evaluation, contained in a 15-page report and based in large part on the doctor's in-person interview with Markle in prison last week.
Markle was charged Nov 5 in a criminal complaint with a single felony count of possessing child sexual abuse images.

According to an FBI affidavit filed with the complaint, the material in question, including two explicit photos of Markle posed with a naked underage girl and other images of him with children in various stages of undress, was found in two Los Angeles storage units.

Commenting on the case at the time of Markle's arrest on Nov 6 at an assisted-living center in Florida, FBI Director ​Kash Patel said Markle had "targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions."
Griffin's ruling capped a competency proceeding set in motion by the judge after Markle's first court hearing on the day of his arrest.

In ordering a psychiatric examination of the defendant, Griffin wrote that she found "reasonable cause" to believe Markle was suffering from some mental deficiency, based in part on his advanced age and "lack of recall" during his first court appearance the day of his arrest.

Dr. Aime Gerodimos, who conducted the evaluation, wrote in her report that Markle appeared to suffer from a "major neurocognitive disorder," possibly the result of mild vascular disease. She also found he was likely "exaggerating deficits" when asked to recall specifics of the allegations against him.

The psychiatrist concluded that Markle "does have sufficient present ability to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him and to assist properly in his defense" — the legal standard for a criminal defendant to be deemed competent.

Markle was first taken into custody at the assisted-living facility where he was residing in Lakeland, Florida, near Tampa. Griffin initially ordered him placed under home confinement on condition that Markle wear an electronic monitoring device.
But days later, the judge revoked the arrangement and ordered him back to jail without bond after Markle cut off his electronic ankle tag with a knife.

It remained unclear when Markle would be transferred to federal custody in California, where the case against him was lodged. The judge on Thursday set a preliminary hearing in the case for Dec 1 in Tampa.

According to the FBI affidavit, federal agents acting on a search warrant earlier this month seized a large cache of slides, film negatives and books from two storage lockers Markle had rented in Los Angeles since 2008.

One of the photos showed a naked girl in a room that appears to be ⁠part of a motel chain in the Philippines, where Markle previously resided and where authorities initiated an investigation of him last month, the affidavit said.

Philippine police said on Wednesday criminal complaints had been filed against Markle in the country’s Cebu province, where he lived. The complaints accuse Markle of violating local laws against online sexual abuse and exploitation of children, police said.
Markle has denied the allegations, telling the Daily Mail the claims were untrue and describing them as "sick lies."

Meghan Markle, an American actor, has been estranged from her father since the run-up to her marriage to King Charles' younger son, Harry, in 2018, when the duchess has said she first became aware of the allegations against her father. She has said she was "deeply distressed" over the matter, which led her to cut off contact between her father and her two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5.

4e9d733d841c4784: KUALA LUMPUR: Five pieces of luggage without security screening stickers raised the alarm that led to the discovery of 96.6kg of drugs in an attempted smuggling operation at the Royal Malaysian Air Force's (RMAF) Subang Air Base on Tuesday.
RMAF chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris said personnel noticed the bags had not gone through the required screening process, prompting further checks.
"An Air Movement Section (AMS) personnel conducting a routine patrol discovered the luggage and a box near the arrival and baggage claim area.
"The five bags were wrapped in plastic and did not bear stickers indicating that they had undergone security screening.
"The accompanying box contained six bottles labelled as chemical fertiliser, which was also prohibited from being carried aboard an aircraft," he told the New Straits Times.

Norazlan said the luggage was subsequently taken to the scanning machine, where security personnel from the RMAF's Air and Ground Defence (Handau) unit detected suspicious packages neatly arranged inside.
"It was also established that the officer was part of the crew operating a logistics flight. He was summoned to open the bags for a physical inspection.
"When informed that the luggage had not passed security screening, the officer allegedly attempted to avoid taking the bags aboard the aircraft and instead returned them to his car," he said.
Norazlan said the Handau personnel refused to allow this and insisted that the bags be opened for inspection.
"As the officer did not have the keys, a Handau personnel assisted in opening the bags using a knife.
"The inspection uncovered torn red packages containing crystal-like substances suspected to be drugs.
"The discovery was immediately reported through the Handau chain of command before the Central Zone Criminal Investigation Branch was alerted," he said.
A subsequent inspection found that the substances were suspected to be crystal methamphetamine.
"We informed the federal police Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department team where they arrived at the scene at 5.20pm to conduct preliminary screening.
"The tests indicated that the substances were positive for methamphetamine, amphetamine and MDMA," he said.
Norazlan said police seized all five bags and the box containing the fertiliser bottles as evidence.
"Two officers were arrested at Subang Air Base, while a third officer was detained at the Labuan RMAF air base on the same day to assist investigations.
"Three other officers and nine other ranks personnel, comprising Handau personnel, provost unit personnel and aircrew, were also taken to a police station to assist investigations," he said.

Earlier, federal police Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police and the RMAF had crippled a drug trafficking syndicate that used military assets, with 11 individuals, including five RMAF officers, arrested in Subang and Labuan.
The arrests followed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's disclosure of alleged involvement by military personnel, including RMAF pilots and officers holding the ranks of lieutenant and captain.

80d110fffb885493: MADRID: Real Madrid have cut the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona down to three points, without the help of Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior, who faces a fight to reclaim his place in the team.

Los Blancos have the chance to pull provisionally level with the Catalan giants on Saturday when they host Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu, with Vinicius in contention to play after serving a four-match domestic ban for hair-pulling.
In Vinicius's absence Jose Mourinho's side beat champions Barca in the Clasico at Camp Nou, as well as scoring wins over Sevilla, Racing Santander and Valencia.

The forward started in Madrid's Champions League victories over AEK Athens and RB Leipzig in that period but without finding the form which made him a vital player for Los Blancos over the past few years.
Vinicius, who joined Real Madrid from Flamengo in 2018, carved out a reputation as one of the most dangerous attackers in world football, helping his side win the Champions League in 2022 and 2024.
However, this season he has struggled badly for form, with his only Madrid goal coming in August against Real Sociedad.
In the interim period, Madrid's record signing, Yan Diomande, has adapted well to his new club and has four goals in his last eight appearances, staking his claim for the left wing spot.
During the international break, Vinicius found some relief with Brazil, led by former Madrid coach Carlo Ancelotti.
The forward seemed unlocked, scoring five times in two friendlies against Japan and Singapore, which he hopes can be a platform to turn his domestic form around.
Vinicius admitted this summer, during which he was heavily linked with a departure from Madrid before ultimately penning a new deal until 2032, he let his standards slip.
Brazil suffered a surprise round-of-16 elimination at the World Cup by Erling Haaland's Norway, which took a toll.

"I don't think I prepared myself as well as I could have after the World Cup because the impact of that tournament is very significant for all Brazilians... being knocked out so early was something we didn't expect," he told reporters this week.
"I used the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years."
Vinicius said speculation on his future led to him feeling "overwhelmed", and he also highlighted the difficulty of staying at the peak of the game.
"I think only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to do it for so many years, reaching the same numbers," he added.
"I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve."
Change of scene
Vinicius's only other goal this season came in the previous international break, for Brazil against Australia in a friendly.
Former Real Madrid player Predrag Mijatovic told Spanish radio station Cadena Ser that Vinicius seems happier playing for Brazil than his club side.

"I think last summer hurt Vinicius quite a bit because he had that doubt about whether to stay or not, whether to renew his contract or not, and he has more competition this year, right?" said Mijatovic.
"Diomande is performing well in this position, and now Mourinho is the one who has to make his own decisions.
"What's clear is that Vini performs well when he's happy, and I see him much happier playing with his national team than playing here."
In previous campaigns the Brazilian has saved his best form for the second half of the season.
"Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals," said Vinicius.
In each of the past five seasons he has netted at least 22 times for Madrid.
On occasion Vinicius has faced criticism and whistles from the team's own fans, but Mourinho has shown patience while urging the most lethal version of the forward to return.
"The Vini who is at his best kills games – like he killed me in the past when I was with Benfica," said the veteran Portuguese coach in September.
Mourinho will hope that Vinicius's joy with Brazil can reignite his club form and bring back that killer instinct.
96647ff8f40d3d74: BANGKOK: Iran goalkeeper Alireza Beiranvand was named Asian Football Confederation Player of the Year at its annual ceremony on Thursday while North Korea's Kim Kyong Yong won the women's award.

The 34-year-old Beiranvand is the first keeper to win the trophy since it was introduced in 1994 and the fifth Iranian named the continent's best player, following Khodadad Azizi, Ali Daei, Mehdi Mahdavikia and Ali Karimi.
He was recognised for his performances at club level with Tractor FC and for the national team.
"Receiving this award is an incredibly historic, unforgettable and emotional moment in my life," said Beiranvand.
"But above all I feel an immense sense of happiness and pride in representing my country. I do not see this award as an individual achievement. It is an honour that belongs to the people of Iran."

Beiranvand won the men's award ahead of Saudi Arabian duo Feras Al-Brikan and Salem Al-Dawsari and was recognised for his performances at the World Cup, where Iran narrowly missed out on a place in the knockout rounds.
Kim became the second player from North Korea to win the women's award after being recognised for her performances in Naegohyang FC's title-winning campaign in the Asian Women's Champions League.
"Now that I have got this award, my dream has come true," she said.
Go Kuroda was named men's coach of the year after steering Japan's Machida Zelvia to the Asian Champions League Elite final, where they lost to the Matthias Jaissle-coached Al-Ahli of Saudi Arabia.
Iran's Marziyeh Jafari retained the women's coaching award for her work with Bam Khatoon in the Asian Women's Champions League.

South Korea's Lee Kang-in was the men's International Player of the Year after featuring for Paris Saint-Germain in their Champions League triumph this year, while Australia's Caitlin Foord won the women's award, having claimed the Champions Cup with Arsenal. - Reuters
d61a13b4ecc20daa: SEREMBAN: The status of Datuk Ismail Lasim's resignation as Negri Sembilan menteri besar will be known after his second audience with Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir today.
Ismail, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, submitted his resignation letter to the Ruler on Monday but continued performing his duties as usual.
Ismail declined to comment on whether his resignation had been accepted or whether he would serve as caretaker menteri besar until a successor was sworn in.
He said the matter would become known after today's audience at Istana Hinggap.
"All will be clear after I have met the Ruler," he said yesterday, after launching the Negri Sembilan Zakat Month organised by the Negri Sembilan Islamic Religious Council.
BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir had earlier confirmed receiving a copy of Ismail's resignation letter.
Negri Sembilan Royal Comptroller Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali said the resignation would only take effect with the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

Constitutional expert Professor Dr Nik Ahmad Kamal Nik Mahmood said the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959 contained no specific provision requiring the menteri besar to obtain the Ruler's consent to resign.
He said the audience was more a matter of palace protocol and courtesy, allowing the menteri besar to formally inform the Ruler of his decision.
Meanwhile, Negri Sembilan Umno has backed Ismail staying on as menteri besar, provided outstanding issues are resolved promptly.
Tampin Umno division chief Datuk Mohd Isam Mohd Isa said the uncertainty surrounding Ismail's position needed to be resolved to ensure the smooth administration of the state government.
He said it was also necessary to allow the State Legislative Assembly to convene and table the 2027 budget before the end of the year.
Ismail was sworn in as the ninth Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar on Aug 2 after the Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional coalition won 25 of the 36 state seats in the state election.
ee0b0cd9888444ed: WASHINGTON: The Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday.

The approvals for 879,000 chip shipments by the Commerce Department included 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent, 43,000 for Baidu, and 4,000 for BYD, all on the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies, the committee noted.

The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the administration of President Donald Trump faces heightened scrutiny following news about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has fueled renewed calls in Washington for a tougher stance on China.

Companies had sought permission to ship over 3.4 million chips to China during the period, the documents showed. It was not immediately clear how many of the approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipments of chips, which included Nvidia's H200 and AMD's equivalent MI325X.

News surrounding Huang has turned a spotlight on instances of Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unpunished, dialing up pressure on the Trump administration to crack down on Chinese tech ​threats.

The Commerce Department said its approach to H200 licensing "is based on a rule published in the Federal Register in January 2026, which imposes significant additional national security-related requirements on license applicants in order to qualify for case-by-case consideration rather than a presumption of denial."

Chris McGuire, a former US official and expert on the US-China technology battle, said, "The fact that over 30% of the AI chips sent to China were shipped to companies that the Department of War has designated as Chinese military companies is astonishing, and calls into question whether Commerce conducted any serious national security review before approving these licenses.”
Nvidia said in a statement that the approvals were "subject to strict conditions and limited volumes." It added that "despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China."
AMD said it "complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations."
Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu, BYD, the Commerce Department and the Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Former President Joe Biden had restricted Chinese access to the prized chips over fears that they would supercharge China's military and erode the US lead in artificial intelligence.

But Trump in December gave the green light for Nvidia to ship its H200 chip to China, rolling back Biden-era restrictions and drawing fierce criticism from China hawks across the US political spectrum.
Despite the approvals, questions swirled as to whether the AI chips were actually reaching Chinese shores.
In May, Reuters reported the US had cleared about 10 companies to buy the H200, but that no deliveries had taken place.

In testimony before the committee in July, Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler said shipments had begun but there had been 'very few.' Several major Chinese internet companies had each obtained about 10,000 H200 chips, Reuters has since reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

"This is the most detailed public disclosure in the history of the Export Control Reform Act," committee Chair Brian Mast, a Republican from Florida, said upon releasing the data, referring to 2018 legislation that expanded Commerce's authority to restrict the export of sensitive technologies for national security reasons.

22e1f5f3bbb8ac76: PETALING JAYA: Perikatan Nasional (PN) chairman Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar says his coalition and Barisan Nasional (BN) must both be willing to make concessions to build political cooperation, particularly ahead of the 16th general election (GE16).
Speaking at Dungun PAS’s 70th anniversary celebration last night, Samsuri said any negotiations between the coalitions must be based on equality, mutual respect and shared interests.
"Don’t expect only us in PN to make concessions. The other side must also be willing to do so," he added.

The BN-PN alliance secured a supermajority in the Melaka state election last Saturday, winning 24 of the 28 state assembly seats – well over the 19-seat threshold. BN secured 21 seats while PN won three.
Following the victory, BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi described PN as a "new strategic partner".
However, a day later, he said BN had no plans yet to extend the cooperation to GE16, adding that discussions on such cooperation would take place in due course.

Zahid’s position differed from that of PAS information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari, who called for both coalitions to begin negotiations immediately, particularly on seat allocations and strategies for GE16.

Samsuri said political cooperation between BN and PN in Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka had shown the importance of all parties being open-minded and willing to compromise when building an alliance.
He also stressed that there was no place for a "big brother" in political negotiations.
"From the outset, I’ve told our negotiating partners that there is no such thing as a 'big brother'. We have to sit down and discuss as equals," he said.
Samsuri said the principles and rules governing negotiations must remain consistent and should not be changed to suit the interests of any particular party.
He warned that failure to reach an agreement could lead to greater political setbacks, especially if the coalitions contest against one another in GE16.
Samsuri said better seat coordination and more structured political cooperation could improve their chances of winning seats currently held by Pakatan Harapan (PH), including those held by DAP.
He added that PN and BN could reclaim several parliamentary seats if they avoided three-cornered contests.
Samsuri also urged party leaders and members to set aside personal interests and positions in pursuit of shared political goals.
"The objective of joining a political party is not to become a candidate at elections," he said.
2b1c5cd9db07944d: PETALING JAYA: Seorang pemimpin Amanah mengulangi pendirian kerjasama politik diperluas kepada parti di luar Pakatan Harapan (PH) termasuk Bersatu, sambil menggesa penjajaran politik baharu berasaskan konsep khemah besar disegerakan.
Setiausaha Agung Amanah, Faiz Fadzil, berkata langkah itu penting untuk membina kerjasama politik lebih luas, khususnya dengan parti yang mempunyai asas sokongan Melayu.
Katanya, kerjasama itu perlu berpaksikan agenda bersama yang jelas, terutama dalam memerangi rasuah, memperkukuh tadbir urus dan mengutamakan kepentingan rakyat.
“Khemah besar itu perlu merangkumi parti-parti lain, termasuk parti teras Melayu seperti Bersatu.
“Penjajaran politik baharu ini perlu disegerakan berasaskan agenda perjuangan sama yang dibawa PH, terutama usaha menentang rasuah.
“Apa jua langkah penjajaran politik ini perlu segera dibincangkan kerana tempoh setahun menuju PRU16 sangat singkat,” katanya kepada FMT.
Beliau mengulas pandangan penganalisis politik bahawa PH wajar melupakan rancangan menjalin kerjasama lebih erat dengan Bersatu susulan prestasi buruk parti itu pada PRN Melaka, minggu lalu.

Bersatu gagal menyaingi Barisan Nasional (BN) dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) dalam merebut sokongan pengundi Melayu pada pilihan raya itu. Begitu juga PH yang hanya menang empat kerusi semuanya oleh DAP.
Bagaimanapun, Faiz berkata prestasi buruk Bersatu berpunca daripada tindakan parti berkenaan bertanding secara bersendirian.
“Kerusi yang dimenangi BN atau PN adalah hasil kerjasama kedua-dua parti. Jika mereka tidak bergabung, PH mungkin boleh menang pada PRN Melaka lalu.
“Sebenarnya, gabungan BN-PN tidak mempunyai hala tuju yang ikhlas dan hanya bertujuan mendapatkan kuasa,” katanya.
Pada 24 Okt lalu, Faiz turut menyuarakan kesediaan bekerjasama dengan parti di luar PH termasuk Bersatu, selagi berkongsi matlamat memerangi rasuah, salah guna kuasa dan ideologi perkauman melampau.
Beliau ketika itu menegaskan pihaknya sentiasa mendukung konsep khemah besar.
8b0553c0fc4c6881: KUALA LUMPUR: A car scrapyard in Jalan Utusan, off Jalan Chan Sow Lin, was 90 per cent destroyed in a fire early today.

Pudu Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Abdul Manas Abdul Wahab said the Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department operations centre received an emergency call at 5.53am.
He said fire engines from the Pudu station and six supporting stations were dispatched to the scene.
"Upon arrival at 6.03am, firefighters found the warehouse engulfed in flames.
"The fire was brought under control at 7.03am," he said in a statement today.
Abdul Manas said firefighting operations were conducted from all four sides of the building using offensive and defensive tactics.
Containment measures were also taken to prevent the fire from spreading to nearby buildings.
A total of 75 firefighters were involved in the operation, which was still ongoing.
A check at the scene found that firefighters were continuing efforts to extinguish the blaze completely.
Further details, including the cause of the fire, are expected to be released after the operation ends.
32ddc820d1efbb64: SHANGHAI: The dollar held near a 19-month high on Friday, having risen over the past eight sessions as jitters over the AI trade sent investors fleeing to safe-haven assets, while the yen steadied after Japanese inflation data.

The dollar index was perched near the 103.9 level, its strongest since early April 2025, and was on track for a fourth straight week of gains. The rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy. Markets are now pricing in a 25-basis-point hike in December and a small chance of a larger move.
The AI trade continued to set the mood, with Anthropic's historic market debut doing little to revive sentiment as US equities fell sharply overnight.

Anthropic notched a valuation of about US$2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, edging past SpaceX's June listing and capping a volatile stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology.

"Risk aversion intensified, supporting the safe-haven dollar and driving demand for US Treasuries," OCBC analysts said in a note. "Investors continued to unwind crowded positions and reassess the macro outlook as Anthropic's record IPO sharpened scrutiny of stretched AI valuations and financing risks."
The US 10-year Treasury yield fell to a one-week low of 5.016% in early Asia trade and is down 10 basis points on the week.

Adding to the dollar's strength were hawkish signals from the Fed. Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday that the evidence did not suggest inflation was heading back to 2% on its own, and that the booming rollout of AI technology could further boost inflation the Fed would have to counteract.

The yen edged up 0.1% against the dollar to 159.50. Data showed Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October, staying above the central bank's 2% target for a second straight month and pointing to broadening price pressures that cement the case for a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

Sterling languished near a one-year low against the dollar at US$1.3094, and the euro struggled near its lowest level since April 2025 and last bought US$1.0972. The Aussie hovered close to a one-year low of US$0.66476.

China's offshore yuan slipped 0.4% overnight, breaking from its recent pattern of calm moves, with no obvious catalyst. China left key benchmark lending rates unchanged in November for an 18th consecutive month.
ee9b0c75e4e564fa: PUTRAJAYA: Seorang penjawat awam ditahan kerana disyaki cuba membawa masuk wanita warga asing secara tidak sah di Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Kuala Lumpur (KLIA) Terminal 2, Sepang, Selasa lalu
Ketua Polis KLIA, M Ravi, mengesahkan menerima laporan berhubung penahanan lelaki berusia 40 tahun itu pada 1.18 pagi oleh pegawai Agensi Kawalan dan Perlindungan Sempadan (AKPS).
